_comment: GPL/LGPL SOURCE-OFFER MIRROR — the reviewed pin table for corresponding source.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Correlix redistributes copyleft-licensed binaries — as
unmodified upstream container images, and inside the images we build ourselves.
GPL-2.0 s3 lets a distributor discharge the source obligation two ways: (a) ship
the corresponding source ALONGSIDE the binary, or (b) ship a written offer good
for three years. Owner decision 2026-09-04 (licence audit D2,
docs/security/LICENSE_AUDIT_2026-09-03.md s4 D2) chose (a) for syslog-ng, and
owner decision 2026-09-05 (tracker 238) generalised it: IF CORRELIX SHIPS THE
BINARY, CORRELIX RETAINS THE SOURCE — however the binary got into the image,
including when it was inherited from an upstream base image and named nowhere in
our Dockerfiles. Upstream availability may be recorded as provenance or used as
the retrieval source, but it is NOT by itself compliance.
TWO SECTIONS.
components[]  Retained corresponding-source artifacts. Each is fetched,
checksum-verified and written into every release bundle's
source-offer/ by scripts/make-installer.sh write_source_offer().
`provides` says which normalized component identities the
artifact satisfies — (package_type, source_package,
upstream_version) — so ONE tarball covers every distro
subpackage built from the same origin, and a different version
matches nothing.
deferred[]    Components with a real source obligation for which Correlix has
NOT yet produced a retained artifact. Explicitly recorded,
version-pinned, dated and REVIEWED. scripts/oci-compliance.py
prints them on every run and FAILS `--release` on them. A
component in NEITHER section fails every mode: silence is never a
pass, and a base-image bump changes the versions so the records
stop matching and a human has to look again.
deferred_source_coordinates{}
For each undischarged Debian obligation, the EXACT source package,
version, URL and Debian-attested sha256 of every file that would
discharge it. Mirroring is then mechanical; the reason it has not
happened is recorded in docs/TRACKER.md, not implied by silence.
verifies its sha256 against the pin below, and writes it to the bundle at
source-offer/<file>. A missing pin, a failed download or a checksum mismatch is
a HARD BUILD FAILURE (scripts/CLAUDE.md s16.1) — an unverified tarball is never
shipped, and 'the network was down' never silently produces a bundle whose
source offer is a lie. scripts/oci-compliance.py reads the same file to decide
whether every copyleft component discovered in a FINAL OCI IMAGE has a retained,
checksum-verified artifact behind it.
ON 'upstream's published sum'. Each entry's `verified_against` states whether
the sha256 is an UPSTREAM-PUBLISHED digest we checked against, or OUR OWN
measurement recorded once and then enforced forever (trust-on-first-use). Those
are different strengths of evidence and the difference is written down rather
than implied, so nobody later mistakes a self-measured pin for a vendor
signature. syslog-ng publishes no checksum at all; busybox does.
ON EXACT CORRESPONDENCE. An upstream release tarball at a matching version is
NOT automatically the source a distribution built: distributions carry patches
and build configuration. `role` and `correspondence` keep that honest — a
`distro-packaging` artifact pinned to the SAME build reference the image's own
package database records (Alpine writes the aports commit into /lib/apk/db) is
what upgrades a component from `upstream-release` to `distro-exact`. Claiming
more than the evidence supports is worse than claiming less.
UPDATING. When a pinned image version changes in deployment/docker, this file
MUST change with it — tests/test_source_offer.py fails the build otherwise.
THE LICENCE REVIEW. scripts/source-review.json holds the per-component licence
determination for every component an image scan could NOT resolve mechanically
(a Debian copyright file is an unordered LIST of licences, not an expression).
Each review names its evidence by path and sha256, states the licences governing
the SHIPPED BINARY, and answers one question: does a corresponding-source
obligation apply? A review that says no turns the component into `not-required`
WITH THE REVIEW AS EVIDENCE; one that says `unclear` stays in manual review; one
that says yes leaves the row in `deferred` below. Every review a `--release` run
relies on must carry `owner_signoff: true` — the owner grants that by editing
that file. A review can never overrule a RESOLVED copyleft expression: that is a
conflict and it aborts the evaluation.
_source_review: scripts/source-review.json — the per-component licence review that decides which of these obligations are real. Read by scripts/oci-compliance.py; a review that says `source_required: false` turns a manual-review component into `not-required` with the review as evidence, an `unclear` one stays in manual review, and every review relied on by a --release run must carry `owner_signoff: true`.

components.name: syslog-ng
components.verified_against: self-measured 2026-09-04 from the canonical GitHub release asset; upstream publishes no checksum, signature or release-asset digest for this file
components.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later (core: lib/, libtest/, syslog-ng/, syslog-ng-ctl/, persist-tool/, tests/loggen/, docker/) AND GPL-2.0-or-later (modules/, scl/) — verified against COPYING at tag syslog-ng-4.7.1
components.notes: No OpenSSL linking exception exists in this COPYING. The stock balabit/syslog-ng image loads all modules, so the running combination is effectively GPL-2.0-or-later. This tarball IS the corresponding source for that image's syslog-ng.

components.name: busybox
components.verified_against: upstream-published sha256 at https://busybox.net/downloads/busybox-1.37.0.tar.bz2.sha256 — fetched and matched byte-for-byte on 2026-09-05. Unlike syslog-ng this is a real upstream attestation, not a self-measurement.
components.license: GPL-2.0-only — BusyBox is explicit that version 2 is the ONLY version; there is no 'or later' option. Verified against LICENSE in the tarball and against the L: field Alpine records in /lib/apk/db/installed.
components.notes: BusyBox is named in NO Correlix Dockerfile. It arrives inside the Alpine layers of nginx:1.27-alpine and is present in every netops-frontend and netops-nginx image we distribute, as the apk packages busybox, busybox-binsh and ssl_client — all three built from this one origin package, so this one tarball is the corresponding source for all three. That invisibility is tracker 238: the licence audit models image REFERENCES and this is a base LAYER. It is found now because scripts/oci-compliance.py scans the FINAL image, not the Dockerfile.

components.name: busybox
components.verified_against: self-measured 2026-09-05 from the canonical GitLab archive of the aports tree at the EXACT commit Alpine records for this package; fetched twice and byte-identical. GitLab publishes no digest for a generated archive, so this is our own measurement recorded once and enforced forever. If a future GitLab archive-format change breaks it, the build FAILS rather than shipping unverified bytes — re-measure deliberately, or serve the retained copy from CORRELIX_SOURCE_MIRROR_DIR.

distro_package.build_ref_source: the `c:` field of /lib/apk/db/installed in the shipped image — the aports commit that built this package. Syft carries it through as syft:metadata:gitCommitOfApkPort, so the claim is checked against the image, not asserted.

components.notes: The upstream tarball alone is not the source Alpine built. This archive is Alpine's complete packaging for busybox at the exact commit the shipped image records: the APKBUILD (which states the build configuration and the sha512 of every input), all 37 distribution patches, and busyboxconfig. Upstream tarball + this archive together are the corresponding source for the binary in the image, which is what lets scripts/oci-compliance.py report correspondence `distro-exact` instead of merely `upstream-release`.

deferred_posture: Correlix has NOT yet produced a retained corresponding-source artifact for this component, and its licence review (scripts/source-review.json, 2026-09-05) concluded that a corresponding-source obligation is real (`source_required: true`) or could not be resolved without a human (`unclear`). Owner decision 2026-09-05 (tracker 238) says upstream availability alone is NOT compliance, so every entry below is a real, open obligation: scripts/oci-compliance.py prints them on every run and FAILS `--release` on them. Clearing one means adding a `components` entry with the upstream source (and, for a distribution package, its packaging archive at the exact build reference) the way busybox and the sixteen 2026-09-05 components were cleared; `deferred_source_coordinates` already names the exact files and their Debian-attested checksums. Removing the component from the image clears it too, which for this residue is the cheaper fix (tracker 260).
_deferred_comment: THE REGISTER OF UNDISCHARGED SOURCE OBLIGATIONS.
GENERATED by `scripts/oci-compliance.py --record-deferred` against the four
images publish-images.yml builds, then reviewed and checked in. It is DATA, not
a decision: recording an obligation here does not discharge it.
WHY VERSION-PINNED. Each row names the exact package version found in the image.
A base-image bump changes those versions, the rows stop matching, and the gate
fails until somebody looks again. A blanket rule ('all Alpine packages are fine')
would hide precisely the class of defect that produced tracker 238 — software
shipped by Correlix that no Correlix inventory could see.
WHAT WAS `license-list` OR `unknown-license`. Debian's copyright files list every
licence appearing anywhere in a source package with no stated relationship between
them, so a scanner cannot tell 'MIT AND GPL-2.0' from 'MIT OR GPL-2.0'. The policy
refuses to guess in either direction. Those 94 components were REVIEWED one by one
on 2026-09-05 against the copyright file (or APKBUILD) the image itself carries;
the answers are in scripts/source-review.json. 33 came back with no obligation and
left this register; 2 came back `unclear` and stay here with needs_human set; 59
came back with a real obligation and stay here until their source is retained.
SOURCE AVAILABILITY DECAYS. base-files was reviewed GPL-2.0-or-later and mirrored
immediately rather than recorded, because the exact versions the images ship
(12.4+deb12u14, 13.8+deb13u5) had ALREADY left the live Debian pool and had to be
recovered from snapshot.debian.org. A recorded obligation is not a safe one.
SOURCE COORDINATES. Every Debian row carries `source_coordinates_ref` into the
top-level `deferred_source_coordinates`, which names the exact source package,
version, base URL and DEBIAN-ATTESTED sha256 of every file that would discharge
it, plus its size. Mirroring is therefore mechanical; the reason it has not
happened is a number — ~228 MB across 38 source packages, in every release
bundle, forever — recorded in docs/TRACKER.md rows 238, 260 and 261 rather than
implied by silence.
